surface: HAL cross-LLM fact-check quorum — is each panelist's MODEL IDENTITY verifiable, or self-reported?
collectedVia: Supabase MCP execute_sql against project qnnpjhlxljtqyigedwkb (hal_classifications schema + rows; information_schema for attestation columns)
foldIn: First fold-in from an analysis of Tencent/AI-Infra-Guard (see docs/AGENTIC-SECURITY-STACK.md): AIG binds a model's identity to an unforgeable attestation (a Claude thinking-signature is an AEAD-encrypted protobuf a relay cannot forge). HAL's BFT quorum assumes N DISTINCT models voted; that independence is only real if each panelist's claimed model can be verified.
note: Read-only schema + aggregate. No prompt text, no answers, no proof bytes. The question judged: can a relay substituting one model for another inside the quorum be DETECTED, or is the model label taken on trust?

per_panelist_record.model_field: SELF-REPORTED free-text string written by the router, e.g. 'fact-check-quorum:llama+glm+gemini+mistral+qwen', 'llama-3.1-8b-instant', 'fact-check-quorum:gemini+mistral'. Not an attested identity — nothing binds the string to what actually answered.
per_panelist_record.integrity_present: previous_entry_hash — a hash CHAIN over the log (tamper-evidence that a row was not altered/removed AFTER the fact). It does NOT attest the model identity: a relay writing model='claude-...' produces a perfectly valid chain link.
per_panelist_record.per_panelist_attestation_column: NONE. No signature, no model-binding token, no attestation field on hal_classifications. Confirmed against information_schema.

sample_quorum.note: 30 panelist rows for one prompt across deepseek/openrouter/trinity-task-bridge, each a self-reported 'fact-check-quorum:<models>' label; log hash-chained; zero per-panelist model-identity attestation.

verdict_level_attestation_exists_but_is_.why_it_does_not_close_the_gap: These attest the OUTCOME/snapshot on-chain (EAS/zkp) — that a verdict was recorded and not tampered. They say nothing about WHICH MODELS produced it. A verdict can be EAS-attested and still rest on a quorum where a relay swapped gemini for a cheaper model; the attestation would sign the swapped result just as happily.

observations.verdict: HAL's per-panelist MODEL IDENTITY is SELF-REPORTED. The log is hash-chained and the verdict is EAS/zkp-attested, but neither verifies that the N claimed models actually and distinctly answered. So the quorum's BFT independence assumption is UNVERIFIED — not breached (no forgery caught), but not checkable either. This is NOT_CHECKED until a per-panelist model-identity attestation is wired.
